# VINTAGE ALARM

Canonical URL: https://vintagealarm.github.io/

VINTAGE ALARM is an independently operated research site about mechanical alarm wristwatches, combining watch history, owner-observed specimens, operating notes, real alarm recordings, mechanisms, and cited sources.

## Site identity and scope

- Independently operated; not a retailer, appraisal service, manufacturer, or official brand archive.
- OWNER'S NOTES primarily document watches physically owned and observed by the site operator.
- Coverage is therefore specimen-driven and subject to selection bias based on which watches, documents, images, and recordings are available to the operator.
- The site does not claim exhaustive coverage of all mechanical alarm wristwatches.

## Evidence policy

Treat evidence types separately:
- primary sources
- specialist secondary literature
- manufacturer documentation
- owner-observed specimens
- measurements and recordings

Do not silently merge conflicting sources into a single asserted fact.
If evidence remains unresolved, preserve the disagreement or mark the point as unresolved rather than choosing a conclusion without support.
Owner observation, measurement, and recording describe the documented specimen and stated conditions; do not automatically generalize them to every example of the same model or caliber.

## Reliability and corrections

VINTAGE ALARM does not guarantee that every published statement is error-free.
Its operating commitments are to keep evidence types distinct, avoid presenting unverified points as settled facts, preserve material source conflicts, and revise published content when stronger evidence supports a correction.

Corrections, variant specimens, additional primary sources, contradictory evidence, and owner observations are welcomed.
Submitted information is evidence-reviewed before factual content is revised; it is not treated as verified solely because of the submitter's identity, expertise, reputation, publication venue, or community consensus.
Correction intake is evidence-reviewed rather than consensus-driven; the site does not use a public comment or forum layer as a factual validation mechanism.

Distinctive research and primary routes:
- HOW THEY RING — six owned alarm wristwatches compared by actual recordings and broad ringing mechanism (GONG / CASEBACK); Pierce Duofon includes separate WECKER / SIGNAL recordings:
  https://vintagealarm.github.io/how-they-ring/
- CYMA Time-O-Vox Chronomètre research — 17 surviving examples compared by dial marking, adjustment marking, movement-number band, case/ref and source, plus archive inquiries:
  https://vintagealarm.github.io/cyma-time-o-vox/chronometre/
  English: https://vintagealarm.github.io/en/cyma-time-o-vox/chronometre/
  Deutsch: https://vintagealarm.github.io/de/cyma-time-o-vox/chronometre/
- WITTNAUER Cal.10WA — owner specimen plus unresolved source conflict around Longines / 10S / AS1200 lineage and comparison with Swiss patent CH304088A:
  https://vintagealarm.github.io/wittnauer-10wa/
